claims.claim: A frozen 16 MB embedding table of 512-bit codes lets a ternary BitNet b1.58 model reach 615-740 tokens per second on a laptop CPU in 62 MB of memory.
claims.episode_span: When paired with a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the entire model fits in 46 MB, ties the float baseline on LAMBADA and PIQA, and runs at 615–740 tokens per second on a laptop CPU in 62 MB of memory—five to six times faster than the float model’s 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at roughly one-seventh the memory.
claims.source_title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
claims.supporting_quote: With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory.

claims.claim: Frontier agents reach at most 49.2% average score and 37.6% joint collaboration score on RealCLI.
claims.episode_span: Frontier agents reach at most 49.2% average score and 37.6% joint collaboration score, with consistent shortfalls in steerability, trust calibration and safety boundary management.
claims.source_title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
claims.supporting_quote: Evaluations reveal profound capability gaps in frontier agents: the best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and when evaluated by the joint collaboration score (J_collab), the peak performance reaches merely 37.6%.

claims.supporting_quote: We construct 96 target languages varying in clause word order, noun-phrase word order, alignment, complement system, and ANC strategy. For each language, we train GPT-2-small models from scratch

claims.claim: Experiments across US, Dutch and Chinese contexts show LLMs over-predict stereotypes and that non-English prompts improve cultural-context consideration.
claims.episode_span: Experiments across US, Dutch and Chinese contexts show LLMs over-predict stereotypes and that non-English prompts improve cultural-context consideration.
claims.supporting_quote: We conduct experiments for US, Dutch, and Chinese cultural contexts. Our results suggest that LLMs do not reliably account for cultural contexts and overpredict the presence of stereotypes. Non-English prompts seem to improve consideration of cultural context

claims.claim: A 141 M-parameter encoder trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a consistent 12-category schema, achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons on AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII at a low-FPR operating point.
claims.episode_span: A 141 M-parameter encoder trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a consistent 12-category schema, achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons on AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII at a low-FPR operating point.
claims.supporting_quote: a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. Evaluated on the AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII benchmarks at a low-FPR operating point, our model achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons
